_README: WHICH KERNEL BOARDS ARE GATES, AND WHICH ARE DISCLOSURES.
public.fn_kernel_all_boards() discovers every board in the estate BY SIGNATURE — any
zero-argument function returning (check_name, expected, actual, ok) — so a new board is watched
the moment it is deployed and nobody has to remember to register it. Twenty-one exist today.
A board not named in this file is a GATE: every check must be ok, and any red fails the suite.
That is the default on purpose. Adding a board here is a deliberate act with a reason attached.
A board named here is a RATCHET: it is a deliberate open-gap report whose red rows are the
disclosure, not a defect to be tuned away. kernel_k6_trace_ledger.sql says so in its own header
— 'every check numerator AND denominator over the FULL table', 'the gap stays visible' — and
demanding zero there would be demanding the disclosure be deleted. What is asserted instead is
that the gap does not GROW: each listed check carries the numerator measured at baseline, and
the suite fails if the live numerator exceeds it. Debt already disclosed is allowed to stand;
new debt of the same shape is not.
kernel_boards_are_green.test.mjs also fails if a ratchet entry no longer matches a real check,
so an entry cannot outlive its subject and silently license a future failure with that name.

2026-08-20 — the fn_phase_d_event_state.event_self_loops ratchet was DELETED, not lowered. D45 replaced that check with self_loop_after_handing_the_work_on, which narrows the subject to the case that would be a defect (a self-loop that does not end its workflow and whose successor step is owned by somebody else) and measures 0. The 54 are still published, as an informational row naming their two components: 15 end the workflow, 39 hand to a successor the same role owns. A ratchet whose check no longer exists silences whatever later takes the name, which is what the guard here caught.

ratchet.why: The seven true orphan traces are preserved ON PURPOSE as the evidence of the defect they record. kernel_k6_trace_ledger.sql, section E: they are annotated with an evidence_ref stating that no task ever carried them, sealed, and deliberately counted in the open rather than filtered out of a denominator. All seven are registered in phase_c_historical_repair as HISTORICAL_ORPHAN_TRACE.

The K4 pointer defect, recorded in kernel_k6_trace_ledger.sql and classified in phase_c_historical_repair as HISTORICAL_STATE_TRACE_MISMATCH. Pre-repair rows kept rather than rewritten, because editing a sealed trace is what the append-only guard exists to refuse.
Same K4 pointer defect, handoff_run side. One row, registered.

Trace 3730, subject_kind trigger_inbox. The trace itself was never edited — fn_phase_c_trace_append_only refuses editing a sealed trace, which is correct — so its subject_kind is exactly as written. It carries an immutable repair relationship: repair_id 83 classified it, repair_id 85 superseded that classification and recorded it as a post-cutover defect that was repaired.

Counts components that have never produced a trace. 430 of the 635 are edge functions, database triggers or event subscriptions, for which this database holds no invocation log at all — fn_kernel_system_trace_state states that explicitly and declines to score them. The number is therefore a coverage-unknown figure, not a defect count, and kernel_k6 keeps it visible under section G rather than filtering it. What IS asserted, on the same board, is that 933 of 933 post-epoch wrapped cron executions carry their required trace and 0 are missing one.
ratchet.owner: open — falls as sources are cut over to the kernel and begin tracing

ratchet.why: edge:inquiry_intake. This read 0 until 18 Aug 2026, on a false basis: the source claimed discharge by routine:trg_inquiry_received, a trigger on public.inquiries, and supabase/functions/inquiry_intake/index.ts never references that table in code — only in two comments. The board resolves the named routine and verifies it reaches the kernel, which is the FAR end of the chain; it never asks whether the source reaches the routine. Correcting the claim moved this 0 -> 1, which is the true number. What the source actually writes is public.customers, a work table with no kernel discharge, and W04 has 0 runs ever. Closing it means wiring W04 — which requires reclassifying dbtrigger:public.customers:trg_emit_customer_registered away from NOT_A_BUSINESS_TRIGGER, registering a new source, and amending customer.registered.allowed_source_systems, after which every signup opens an onboarding run with an owner and an SLA. That is a founder decision, not a wiring fix. CLOSED 2026-08-25: the one source it named, edge:inquiry_intake, carried disposition_evidence that split_part could never parse (it began "measured 2026-08-18:"), so the row fell through to this count — correctly, because the customers write it describes really had no kernel discharge. phase_d_q03 built that discharge and phase_d_q05 wrote the claim in the keyed shape the parser requires. The ceiling is 0: a new bypass now fails rather than fitting under an old allowance.
ratchet.owner: CLOSED 2026-08-25 — held at 0. phase_d_q03 discharged the public.customers write at the TABLE for all eleven edge functions that make it; phase_d_q05 corrected the three coverage claims that were unreadable by the routine that judges them.

ratchet.why: PHASE D DISCLOSURE. It counts how many of the 257 steps have PRODUCED their declared effect at least once in a COMMITTED execution. It reads 257 because no committed business arrival has yet driven a step to a persisted effect, not because the path is broken. That distinction is now measured rather than argued: E12 and E14 fixed the two orderings that made every dispatch refuse, and scripts/checks/phase_d_dispatch_reaches_executed.test.mjs drives all 30 workflows through fn_kernel_workflow_start, fn_kernel_step_complete, fn_kernel_handoff_accept and fn_kernel_review_decide in execution_context production and asserts at least one EXECUTED with a matching phase_d_effect_ledger row. Measured 2026-08-20 after E19: 254 dispatch rows, 2 EXECUTED (W01-S05, W21-S08), 2 ledger rows, residue 0, ai_cost_log delta 0, active cron delta 0. THE PRIOR TEXT OF THIS ENTRY WAS WRONG ON TWO POINTS AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It said the number CANNOT fall to 0 under the current holds; a step can now reach EXECUTED, so what holds the number is the absence of a committed arrival, which is a different and smaller claim. It also said the only driver is fn_phase_d_drive_workflow, which D36 made false by wiring the dispatch into both kernel openers, and which fn_phase_d_effect_reachability repeated on 144 of 257 rows until E15 made that column read an actual dispatch attempt and label anything else CONTRACT_PRECONDITION_NOT_YET_OBSERVED. What genuinely holds the remainder, per that function: 21 steps are held closed by the capability boundary while paid inference waits for Phase E (the founder to lift); 125 write a business object and fn_phase_d_effect_produce refuses rather than choosing a business_key and owner_ref the caller did not supply, which is deliberate and is the auto-vivification defect being prevented; the rest need applicable hard rules to be given facts about a business subject that does not exist while the business tables sit at zero. NOTHING WAS COMMITTED TO MOVE THIS NUMBER, and nothing should be: a ledger row created by a probe would be a row added to make a count look better. Delete this entry when a real arrival drives it to 0, do not lower and leave it.
ratchet.owner: OPEN — the capability and provider holds are the founder's to lift; the rest waits on a committed business arrival, which Phase D deliberately does not manufacture.
ratchet.measured_at: 2026-08-20, 257 of 257 committed. Driven probe after E19: 254 dispatches, 2 EXECUTED, 2 ledger rows, all rolled back.

ratchet.why: E34 made this a real red. It read "4 of 4" with its ok column written as the literal true, so four amendments to FROZEN Phase C kernel contracts sat live in production, unapproved, under a fully green board. The ok is now computed from the population it reports. The condition is genuinely unmet and this is the honest colour: an amendment to a frozen contract is not complete until the person who froze it has approved the change. PCCR-001 and PCCR-002 are written, tracked and registered with their section 11 unsigned. Nothing in this repository may clear it — approved_by and approved_at are constrained to move as a pair, and a builder writing his own name into them is exactly the defect this row exists to surface. Lower max_numerator as he signs; delete the entry when it reaches 0, do not silence it. | 23 Aug 2026: cleared to 0. All five amendments now carry an approval recorded through fn_phase_c_freeze_amendment_approve inside a verified founder session (auth.uid()); the ratchet is lowered so the gain cannot be given back.
ratchet.owner: the founder — his signature on docs/phase-c/PHASE_C_CHANGE_REQUEST_PCCR-001.md and PCCR-002.md section 11

ratchet.why: F31 added this row, and it is red on purpose. public.phase_c_freeze_amendment could not tell an approval the founder placed through a verified session from one a migration wrote on the strength of an instruction he sent in writing — both leave the same string in approved_by. Amendment 36 (PCCR-003) is the second kind: phase_d_f23_pccr_003_recorded_and_approved.sql put his email and now() into the row, quoting his ruling of 21 Aug 2026 section E verbatim in its own header, and approved_at equals the instant the change request was raised, which no human signature ever does. His instruction is real and is not deleted — deleting it would lose the thing he actually gave. What is disclosed is WHICH KIND it is, in a column constrained to move with approved_by and on a board row nothing in this repository can clear. It goes to 0 when he approves PCCR-003 himself through the verified-subject door F20 built and F21 granted. Delete this entry then; do not lower it. | 23 Aug 2026: cleared to 0. All five amendments now carry an approval recorded through fn_phase_c_freeze_amendment_approve inside a verified founder session (auth.uid()); the ratchet is lowered so the gain cannot be given back.
ratchet.owner: the founder — an approval through a verified auth subject, replacing the one recorded from his written instruction

ratchet.why: One row: fn_phase_d_run_injected_defects -> phase_c_task. PD-TRACE-004's half (c) DELIBERATELY attempts `update public.phase_c_task set trace_id = <a trace deleted in this transaction>` in order to find out whether the task-side orphan can be staged at all. It cannot: the attempt is refused 42501 by fn_kernel_write_guard because no routine with write authority for that table is on the call stack, and the branch records exactly that as its observation. The board is right that a statement which will be refused at runtime is sitting in a deployed routine; here that IS the measurement. Granting the probe authority would defeat the refusal it exists to measure, and removing the attempt would leave a prose-only assertion in its place, which the founder's section 4 forbids. Any SECOND unauthorised writer still turns this red.
ratchet.owner: open by design — the Phase D injected-defect probe, fixture-context only, aborted transaction

ratchet.why: phase_d_q03 added this row so the source inventory stops being silent about its own completeness. public.kernel_trigger_source holds 25 edge functions; public.phase_c_edge_function_writes measures 143 that write at least one table, and 52 of the uninventoried ones write a WORK table. Every correction phase_d_q03 made to the eight false-positive bypass rows rests on the sentence "the write happens in the edge function, which is inventoried separately", and that sentence is only worth something if the inventory is complete. It is not, so the number is published rather than assumed. It is a RATCHET and not a gate because closing it means classifying 52 functions from what each one does, which is measurement work nobody may guess at; it may not GROW, and the eight of the 52 that write public.customers are covered regardless by z50_customer_registered_kernel_emit on the table.
ratchet.owner: open — Phase C kernel cutover, source inventory completeness increment

ratchet.why: PCCR-006 created public.phase_c_governance_decision and this board row on 25 Aug 2026, and the row reads 1 of 1 from its first moment. The one is PCCR-003 -- the founder approval of 21 Aug 2026, approved_by management@quotesdone.com, approved_at 2026-08-21 20:20:33+00 -- which has an approver and no governance_decision_id because the ledger did not exist when he gave it. Closing it would mean minting a ledger row for a decision that predates the ledger: inventing the verified session it never had, which is the exact defect PCCR-006 exists to close. It is REFUSED, not deferred. The same row is grandfathered by phase_c_change_request_approval_is_derived NOT VALID, whose migration asserts the grandfathered set is exactly PCCR-003 and fails if a second appears. The ceiling is 1: any NEW approved change request without a verified governance decision fails this check, and every approval after PCCR-006 must come through fn_phase_c_governance_decide, which refuses any connection whose session_user is not authenticator.
ratchet.owner: CLOSED-BY-DESIGN -- historical, preserved as evidence. It cannot reach 0 without fabricating a decision record, and it must not.
